- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes (especially >80), leading to overcorrection; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85 multiplier) to peak forecasts.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum shifts; weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) more heavily in smoothing or trend adjustment.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.0, 0.3, 1.0), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to forecast adjustments.
